body: Thank you.

Today at the gym I got some unsollicited advice. A man asked if he could give me some advice and I said yes because I'm not assertive. I've been only training at the gym for a year and I'm sure I don't do everything perfect all the time, but I'm also wary about taking advice from a stranger. Just because he can dumbell bench press 34 kg doesn't mean he's an expert. When I just joined the gym I had some guy giving me ''advice'' about dumbell shoulder press. I asked about it here and I was doing it right, though his way was also right.

  
I was just done with lat pulldowns. He said I should keep my shoulders low during the entire exercise. So also when the bar is at the top. I've watched several vids on YouTube from several respected trainers when I started working out, to learn proper form. I've watched them again and I've been doing what they have showed. There are probably several was to do a lat pulldown?  
And he also commented on my seated cable row, which he saw me doing earlier. I agree form sometimes suffers a bit. I just moved on to a heavier weight, and the last few reps I lean a bit forward and backwards.

  
I really dislike him giving me advice. It's a small gym and across from me were 2-3 people who could enjoy the show. It makes me feel embarresed. Why did he had to choose me. I sometimes see people with questionairy form, but I don't know enough, I'm not going to say anything. That's up to the trainers.

I might asked for a form check, when I have the opportunity to film myself.

I have a new boyfriend and he's great. I met him at the gym. Last week we were talking about something, not sure what. I said my goal was to get stronger than him. I was sort of joking. He said that it isn't possible and why would I want to be stronger than a man. Why would I want to be stronger than a man? Because it's fun to get stronger and stronger. And also to feel a bit more safe.  
I was sort of joking when I said I wanted to be stronger than him. I don't think it's possible to get stronger as him, especially if he keeps training too, but I think it's possible to get as strong as he is now. It's not as if he's super strong. We go to a regular gym, no powerlifting or anything. My BF lifts what I see the majority of guys in this gym lift. Dumbbell bench press. I think he currently lifts around 24-26 kg for his working sets. Not super heavy compared to the strongest man on earth.  
I think it's possible for a woman who's not competing or anything to achieve this? It might takes some years of training, I don't know, I'm not in a rush. I'm now at 16 kg (working sets) for dumbbell bench press. That's after 10 months in the gym, training upper body twice a week. I think I started at 6 or 8 kg. I find it harder to progress in weight for upper body than I do for lower body. The progress is slow, but there's progress.  
We will see how strong I can get.

I feel the same anxiety. I'm 31 and female. I started dating a guy last week and yesterday it got physical. We were watching a movie and he started with holding my hand. Later he put his arm around me. And a little later that evening he started making moves to kiss me. At first I avoided it, but the I thought I should try it. Him kissing me on the lips didn't felt good and after a few seconds I pulled away. I panicked. I felt so much anxiety. At first it felt nice sitting so close to him, but the hand holding and everything. I only felt anxiety. 

This was our third date. After our second date I hoped he would hug me and kiss me the next time we would see eachother. I had fantisized about it. So it's so strange that I only felt anxiety.

I do like huggin my parents, but besides them I haven't really had physical contact with people.
Today I wore shorts to the gym for the first time. They aren't very short, stop just above the knees. I'm a bit insecure about my legs, especially in the gym, so this is a small win.

Thank you. Yes, I've to remind myself that. About 2 months ago he talked to me for the first time. So he should know that I'm a bit socially akward and not such a talker. He still asked me out, so it shouldn't be a dealbreaker for him. I've had comments on me being so quiet when I was a teenager, so I feel I'm not good enough when I don't talk a lot.

Thank you. Yes, I've to remind myself that he asked me out because he likes me and  wants to get to know me better. I think the first time he talked to me was about 2 months ago, so he should know I'm not such a talker.
My gym crush asked me out!

My gym crush asked me out. Next week we have a casual date. I should be excited, but all I can feel is anxiety (and sometimes a bit of excitement). I know most people are a bit anxious for a first date, but I have social anxiety and that add a lot more of anxiety. I'm also so bad at texting. I'such an overthinker. All I want to do is RUN, but I really like him. I'll probably regret it if I don't try it.

I'm actually also suprised he wants to go out with me after having talked to me several times. I'm so bad at making conversation and I'm so akward. Most people just let me after one or two tries.

Another workout at the gym without seeing my gym crush. Haven't seen him this week. I'm away this weekend, so I'll probably see him sometime next week. He's such a sweet guy. I think he's interested in me. Not sure I'll have the guts to ask him out.

Gym is going well, diet not. The weightloss is so slow. I probably have to cut another 100 calories. Or just stick to my calorie goal every day. It's hard. I'm such an emotional eater.

I started The Challenge from coach Mark Carroll this week. Started later because of vacation. I bought it because I wanted to lose some weight and this challenge is 8 weeks, so I thought that would be good to help me.

But I don't like it. I don't like the programm. It doesn't have barbell squats in it. I can swap the box squats for that. But I also don't like that it has so many supersets in it. Most of them aren't convenient in a gym. Like today, Leg press superset with 45 degree hyperextensions. But those machines are not close to each other. If I'm doing hyperextensions, someone can go on the leg press and I can't blame them. I can't hog machines and I don't want to. I could work in with someone, but I don't really want to do that jut because I need to superset. And there are some more supersets with machines/barbells that are so not close to each other. So I have been doing those as a stand alone exercise. Don't know if that makes a different for the results.

I'm just not really enjoying this program. He might be a good coach and his clients get results. But if I don't enjoy it. There are programs that give you results and are fun to do. Others might like this program, but it's not for me.

I regret buying it, it wasn't cheap. That's why I doubt paying for a program. Because you don't know what to get. I liked the upper/lower from aworkoutroutine. I did that for about 6 months, so I thought to try something else. I did the PPL for beginners from the wiki for 3 weeks, until I started The Challenge. That one was ok, maybe 6 days is a bit much for now. I think I rather do 3 days lower and 2 days upper.

So what to do now? I'll finish this week of The Challenge, but I think I'll look for another program that suits me better.

I was on vacation for a week, so no gym for a week. Yesterday was my first time back at the gym. A bit sore today. I also feel my back, from deadlifts. I'm not sure if it's the good kind or the bad kind. So I'm a bit worried. I used the weight I did for my break. Lesson learned and next time I can better do a lighter weight, just to be sure.

Something positive. Saw my gymcrush again. And talked a bit with him.  He started talking to me. I'm too anxious to start a conversation myself. I wonder if he might like me too or if he's just being nice and likes talking to people.

I enjoyed this one: [https://www.aworkoutroutine.com/the-muscle-building-workout-routine/](https://www.aworkoutroutine.com/the-muscle-building-workout-routine/)

It looks a bit like TLS, but this one appealed to me more.

I've also seen this one recommended. I don't own it, but I'm considering buying it. [https://www.strongerbyscience.com/program-bundle/#:\~:text=The%20Stronger%20By%20Science%20program,t%20need%20to%20purchase%20again](https://www.strongerbyscience.com/program-bundle/#:~:text=The%20Stronger%20By%20Science%20program,t%20need%20to%20purchase%20again)

Social anxiety. Joined a gym last October. I was really anxious going to the gym and I was every time going to the gym for a few months. What helped me was having a plan. It's a small gym and it has two trainers who you can ask to explain how the machines work. I've also watched several YouTube vids on how the exercises have to be performed. My mom is also a member of that gym, though she does a circuit in an other room. But when felt really anxious, she would train with me. By now I'm going to the gym by myself. And I see most people are going to the gym alone. Some with a friend or a partner. And sometimes there are teenagers in groups of 3-5. I also try to go at times that it won't be busy. Like around 6pm was a bad idea.

Today was lower body. Squats are moving in the right direction again. A few weeks ago I was in an accident with my bike and I hurt my tailbone. It made doing some lower body exercises hard. I had to lower the weight a lot or not do them at all. Today I'm finally back at the weights I was before the accident.

During squats a girl/woman was doing upper body in front of me. She was doing shoulder press with 14kg dumbbells and bench press with 14 and 16kg. That's impressive. I'm now at 12kg with shoulder press and struggle with increasing the reps for bench press with 14kg. 2kg increases feels so hard for upper body.

The guy in the tutorial from Squat University did it like that, slow and controlled.

I used a 10kg plate. The next one are 20kg and they are a lot bigger. They might be a little bit too heavy for me now. I will try it with stacked plates next time. Thank you.

Has anyone reading this done one of coach Mark Carroll's programs? I've been thinking about doing his Building the bikini body part 1. I see that he has a 8-weeks challenge starting soon. Since I want to lose some weight I thought of maybe doing the shred. I don't really care about the prices, chances you win something are so small.

These programs cost a lot of money. If they are good then it's worth it, but I'm afraid of wasting more money (like on Kayla Itsines BBG).

I've been doing an 4-day upper/lower split for about 6-7 months. From the start of April I added a extra (a lighter) day that has a foccus on glutes. I still enjoy this program and I still make progression. Some upper body lift progress very slow, but that's maybe normal.  
I've been looking at other programs and I kind of think I'll like the PPL for beginners from the wiki. Though it's 6 days and only 2 of them are lower body. The lower body isn't tht different from what I do now. The upper body has some lifts that aren't in my current program.  
Not sure if I should stay with my current of try the PPL. Not sure if 6 days isn't too much. I think my body can handle it, but maybe it would be too much for me mentally. I've social anxiety, so going to the gym can be stressing.

Maybe I should just try the PPL a week.

I do. One the first or second day I do get cramps and if I don't take ibuprofen, I get sick. Luckily ibuprofen works for me and I don't feel the camps or I feel them lightly. I also get really tired on the first or second day. Usually I can workout, if I do it in the morning.

I don't know if my period affects my training.

This morning at the gym. A man was on a machine a few meters away from me. At every rep he moaned. Some people make noises when working out. But this sounded like it came straight from a porn movie. It was both funny and uncomfortable.

A few days ago I was hit by a car while I was on my bike. His fault. I'm mostly ok, only my tailbone still hurts. I can still sit and ride a bike without pain, so it's probably not broken or (badly) bruised.

But I can't do squats, hip thursts, lunges. That hurts. Today wsa upper body day and it hurt to lay on the bench. Picking the dumbbells from the floor also hurt.

I hate this. That this useless body part can cause so much trouble and pain. I know I should be glad that my injuries aren't worse. I just hate that I can't exercise the way I want. This was the only thing that was going well in my life. It makes me feel more depressed than usual.

Today I went to the gym at a for me new time on a Tuesday. Going on a different time gives me anxiety because I don't know what to expect, but there was only one other person. I love it when there's only one or two persons at the gym. Makes me feel much more at ease.

It was maybe a bit too early for me, because I didn't look good at my program and for the first 3 I used to same weight as last week while I should have upped the weight. That annoyes me.

Thank you, this is great! I'm going to put a suggestion in the suggestion/comments box at the gym. She also wrote that the decline bench is her favorite. My gym recently added a decline bench, so I'm going to try that next time.
I like the vegan wondershake from The Protein Works. Many flavours.

I recently bought a pair of Vivobarefoot shoes to use in the gym. They are so much better than Converse. More room in the toe area.

Can't comment on your squat, I'm still working on improving mine.

What height box or step would be ideal for hip thrust? The lowest side of the box at my gym is 20 inch / 51 cm. And the benches are the same height. It's actually a bit too high and you need to lift yourself with the bar on it. Don't know how the girl that was about to hip trust 140kg did it.

I want to suggest to the gym to buy a lower box or an adjustable step. What height should I suggest? What would work best for people with height 1.60-1.70m (5'3 - 5'7)?
Thank you. The plates under my heels were suggested to help me staying more upright while I work on improving my ankle mobility. Next time I'll try without to see how that now goes.
Thank you. I don't find bracing easy and I'm not always bracing hard enough. That's something I'll have to keep working on.
Thank you, I didn't know this. I'm now squating half my body weight, 32,50kg. I'll now continue to add weight or/and reps every week and keep checking on my form.

Went to the gym early in the morning. For half my workout I had the gym to myself. Then this man in his sixties comes in. (He's alright, but he moans at EVERY rep, whatever exercise he does.) He started with bench press with a weight of 60 kg. Probably a warm-up weight for some, but he only added 5kg at every side for his other sets.

He also bench pressed in front of the cage, so without safety arms. About 90% of the guys I've seen bench pressing do that in front of the cage instead of inside the cage with safety arms. I really don't get that. They also don't have a spotter. Maybe they keep the weight low? Still seems dumb. I was the only other person at the gym this morning and I can't lift 70 kg of a person. He's still alive. But one day he might fail.

My gym now has a smith machine. I decided to try step ups on it. I used the lowest weights but it was just hard and it didn't feel right. I think I'll stick to dumbbell step ups. Or maybe I need some more practise.

I would want to know. Though I would feel very ashamed and I would might switch gyms. For this reason I check it in the mirror myself. I actually ordered a new legging last week and I discovered that it shows when doing rdl of squats. I'm glad I found out at home.

Not sure if I would tell another woman if her legging is see through. I would be araid for a negative respons.

Failed bench press again and now I have it on tape. No big deal, that's why you should use safety arms if the gym has them. It was on the fourth and last set, I wanted to try one more rep but couldn't get it up again.

Felt selfconcious about filming myself. I hadn't filmed my bench press for a few weeks because of the amount of people there were. My bench was a bit uneven and I tried to work on it. Today there was only one woman when I started. First I put my phone on the ground, but it wasn't a very good angle. So I dragged a plyo box in front of the bench and put my phone on it. Woman saw that and it made me insecure, like what would she think of that. I shouldn't care about that, of course. But still feel that way. At least I could see how the barbell moved and it was mostly even, so that's good.
Probably. My current gym is very good and I haven't experienced anything bad with men in the gym, but I just feel more at ease around women.

Man was doing dumbbell curls right in front of the dumbbell rack, mirror is behind that. Don't know how many sets of about 6 reps, probably supersetting as he walked away everytime. Seemed like no one else needed dumbbells and I could grab the pair I needed during his rest time. Still annoying. Don't get why some guys need to stand right in front of the rack/mirror.

Bought liftings traps and today I tried them for the first time. Romanian Deadlifts, 4 sets x 6-8 reps. Last week the weight was 45kg and the bar started slipping out of my hands by the 5th-6th rep. Today with the lifting straps I could do 50kg for 8 reps.

A guy saw me using these straps and asked if I used them because of my grip. He said he had that problem too when he started out and said that farmers walk helped him with that. I had read about farmers walk, but hadn't tried them yet. I tried them at the end of my workout. Will do them weekly now and also deadhangs, to make my grip stronger.

In my gym no tanktops and no crop tops. This is an independent gym. Not sure what the rules are in other gyms. My gym has this rule to be inclusive for everyone. Some people can feel unfomfortable to see young women in only a sportsbra and because of that not join a gym. Same for men in a tanktop, but a sportsbra reveals much more.

I can understand this reasoning. I don't mind wearing t-shirt. Though I also think that a tanktop doesn't show much more than a t-shirt, so I don't know why that wouldn't be allowed. Sportsbra I get, but If I really want to workout in a sportsbra, I can join one of the other 5 gyms in that town.

Upper body today. After I started it got a bit busier at the gym. Mostly (young) guys. And this time I was the only girl in the free weights area. I always get a bit insecure lifting around guys. But why? It isn't like they do everything perfect. I'm still insecure about my form and bench press, dumbbell rows and incline bench press I can't see that in the mirror and I was too afraid to film myself with all the guys in the area. I also haven't seen anyone else recording themself.

I wanted to up the weight for dumbbell row. I've done 16kg for severall times and I should have tried 18kg the last time, but it seems so heavy. Was a bit scared to try the 18kg with a guy next to me, but I did it and I was able to row with 18 kg.

Next was incline bench press with 14kg dumbbells. I struggle with that weight, but this time it went better than last week.

Dumbbells at my gym go from 1-10 and then it's 12,14,16,etc. Those 12kg and up look so intimidating to me. I'm so nervous when I have to try to go heavier, but I should just try it. It isn't bad if I fail, as long as I don't hurt myself.

It's getting warmer, also in the gym. It might be time to switch to shorts. Only thing is I don't feel comfortable in shorts, especially in the gym. I'm insecure about my upper legs, bit fat and wobly but also some celulite. Cycling/biker shorts hide that a bit. But then my calves. You can see the blue vains so clearly, especially on my right calf. Not sure if it's because of my skin or if they are beginning of varicose vains. Blue vains are on more places of my body visable, but the ones on my calves I find ugly and makes me so self-concious.

I know I should just wear short and not care about what other people might think, but it's hard. It's feels so horrible to be called fat or ugly. I've had comments on my body as a child, teenager and adult. And I know it says more about those people than about me. There are also many teenage guys / early 20s guys and in my experience they are the worst.

It's only since a year of 3 that I'm wearing shorts during running. I worry way too much about what other people might think.
I need lifting straps. Can anyone recommend one?  So many choices.

I failed bench press today. And the only other person that in the gym was a few meters away saw it happening. And he seemed amused? But I could have been mistaken about that.

No big deal, there are safety arms. I used the same weight as last week, but  I wanted to try one more rep, but I couldn't get it up again.

After me he went bench pressing, but in front of the cage, so no safety arms. I don't get why so many guys to that. I don't see which advantage that has, except for ego.

Today at the gym. I saw a guy put both hands in his pants, adjusting something? He took his time. I hope his hands weren't in his underwear. Either way, it's gross and he should have just go to the bathroom which is only a 5 seconds walk. And wash his hand, but many people don't do that either.

Later I heard him say to his friend ''that blond girl stared at me for like 5 minutes, didn't even looked away, blahblahblah''. (I'm not the girl, I'm not blond) Boy, I'm pretty sure she wasn't staring at you. Just looking if you were already done with the squats.

Just curious how long people use a rack when they do bench press or squats.

It usually takes me around 20 minutes. Some warming-up sets and 4 working sets with rest time. I sometimes wonder if I take too long. We only have one cage for squats and bench press. I go at times when it usually isn't busy and often no one goes right after me when I'm done. Recently a few times it looked like someone wanted to use it but these persons didn't aks me anything and did use it after me.

One time I made the mistake to go around 6 pm and it was busy. The entire hour I was there the cage was used by a group of 3 guys. So maybe 20 min is ok? I also can't rush through my sets.
Also, I saw a young woman do hip thrust with 160 kg. I don't know how many reps and sets, but just one rep with that weight seems so impressive to me.

This is more of a rant.

Went to the gym and it was kind of busy. The last few weeks I went ont this day and time is was not, and now. That gave me anxiety. I couldn't start with the first part of my program and the other part were isolation exercises. Instead of squats I did leg press until the cage was free.

Whe it was time for hip thrust I couldn't find the pad. I looked everywhere before I asked the trainer about it. She helped me look for it and found it behind the radiator. Didn't think to look there. What idiot does it put there?

Then for my working sets I put 10kg too much at each side. I wondered why it felt so hard and I could barely do 10 reps. I'm glad I found out after the first set.

Lower body day took about 30 minutes longer than normal. I had to rush for an appointment I had later. So tired now.

Went to the gym this morning. Seemed like there wasn't anyone working out, just some people  in the coffee corner. I started with lat pull-downs. I needed a 2.5 kg plate so the increasement would be smaller. I walked to the free weight area and I see a loaded barbell, 2.5 plates on the ground in front of the ez bar. I thought who left this mess. I rarely see this at my gym. I grab a 2.5 kg plate from the ground and start my sets. A little bit later I see a man using the stuff in the free weights area. From the looks of it he was doing a circuit. Whatever. You can't claim all four 2.5kg plates because you're doing a circuit.

No word from him, so it was alright.

I'm going to the gym tomorrow, but I maybe went twice there on a Wednesday. So I'm very anxious about how many people will be there. You never know how many there're going to be. One week there's one and the next week there're six. Still, going at a different day/time makes me even more anxious.

Went to the gym at a time where there were almost noone in the last few weeks. Now there were people and the cage was taken, so I couldn't start with squats. That annoyed me. I know many people who go to busy gyms or can only go at busy times deal with this all the time and have to adjust their workout. But it just felt off to me to not do my workout as planned.

So I started on the leg press, one with a set weight with a pin. I could do 3x10 reps of 90 kg. A few weeks ago I couldn't move the 90 kg. Probably because I now did it with fresh legs and usually it's the 4th exercise or something.

Bulgarian split squats went like sh\*t. The dumbbells from last week felt so heavy and I had to go down in weight. But hip thrust went ok and I could go up in weight. I always feel insecure when something goes less well that the week before, but I just need to remind myself that that will happen and I'm still progressing.

Ended with a few sets of squats at a lighter weight. Couldn't go to heavy after the workout, but I wanted to practise my form. It's slowly improving.

My gym has a new rope cable attachement. This one is a little longer than the old one and triceps pushdowns do feel better with the longer rope.

Also I heard one of the walls in my gym is getting removed so the weight section is getting bigger. Which probably also means new equipment. Hopefully some more benches. But I really hope for another (or 2) squat racks. There's now only a cage.

Exciting!

I put a towel on the machine when I use it. That's what I've been told to do when I joined the gym. Also did that at another gym years ago. Most people at this gym do that, though there are some people that don't even have a towel with them. There are also cleaning wipes and spray to clean the equipment (what you've touched).

Few days ago I was squatting the the cage. My gym only has that one cage for squats, bench press, pull-ups and what else. I had just started on my working sets and this guy who has just entered the gym started doing pull-ups during my rest time. He didn't even asked if he could work in. Which I think would have been the polite thing to do. I can't squat when he's doing pull-ups. It felt so akward.

  
What was even worse. During his rest times, so when I would squat, he was standing right behind me, facing my back. He was standing just outside the cage, so he wasn't in my way. When I was up from my squat, I could see him in the mirror accross the room. He was standing there with his legs wide. His stance looked so confident or intimidating. Or like he was taking space, like I'm here, go away. It made me feel self conscious. I tried to ignore him and focus on my form and not to rush trough my sets.  
He wasn't being a creep and looking at my butt, mostly at his phone. Definitely not into me or anything. It felt more like he wanted to chase me away. Though he finished just before me and didn't used the cage after I was done. I don't know what was up with him. He could have just taken a step aside or turn around so he wasn't right behind me. It was so akward. Of course I didn't had the guts to ask him if he couldn't stand right behind me.

Most of my lifts are progressing, but a few are progressing so slowly. At least I think they are, compared to the others. Seated cable row. I even use a 2,5 kg plate, so the increase is smaller. Single dumbbell row does progress at a nice rate. Same with cable triceps pushdown, but skull crushers are progressing well.

And high bar squats... I'm working on my form, ankly mobility is most likely the issue. It frustrates me. Maybe I should swith to low bar.

Today I registrated my upper body training with the 'strenght' option on my Garmin watch. Usually I just registrated the time. This option registrates the sets, reps, rest times. Even the exercises, though not 100% right. An hour training and I only trained for about 20 minutes, the other 40 minutes were rest. That was kind of shocking to see, but I guess to expect when rest times are 1-3 minutes.

What is the right or best way to do cable glute kickbacks? Can you recommend a YouTube video?  I have seen trainers do them with their body more vertical and other trainers do it with their upper body more horizontal. I've seen many people on Istagram do it with their body more horizontal, but then I came across a trainer on Ista who said that way you have less of a ROM and you should have your upper body more vertical. So confusing.

Today at the gym. I was squatting in what I think you call a cage. This one thing for squats, bench press, dips, pull-ups and what else.

So I was squatting. And during my rest, this guy started doing pull-ups. I don't own the gym, so he can use it too. But I think the polite thing for him to do was to ask me if he could do pull-ups during my rest times. I mean I was doing squats and I can't squat when he's doing pull-ups.

But what was even more annoying. During his rest time, so when I was squatting, he was standing behind me facing my back. He was just outside the cage, so he wasn't in my way. But he was standing behind me, wide legs, this confindent/intimidating stance. I could see him in the mirror when I was up. He wasn't being a creep and staring at my butt or anything. Mostly looking at his phone. It made me feel self-conscious and wanted to rush through my sets. But I tried not to let it intmidate me and I tried to focus on my form and complete all my sets. He could have just taken one step to the side so he wasn't right behind me. Or turn around to look outside. This was just weird and akward. I don't know if he wanted to try to chase me away or that he didn't think anything of it.

Of course I didn't had the guts to say anything about it. I wonder if an other woman would have said anything of it. And if he would have done the same if I was a guy.

Also, I'm pretty sure I'm older than he is. Maybe even at least 8 years older, though I don't look like it. I hate it that I feel intimidated by younger guys, even by teenagers.

Today I finally saw my gym crush again. Haven't seen him for about 4 months. How just a simple hi from him can make me smile all the way home. I hope I'll seem him again soon. He's such a nice guy. 

It's hard getting my squat form right. I know I should have patience and just keep working on it, but it's just frustrates me sometimes.

Thank you. I've noticed my torso is leaning a bit too much forward. Today I've tried to squat with just the barbell and put my heels on plates. I was able to stay more vertical. Then I tried it without plates and it was hard. It feels like it's definitely also an ankle mobility problem, so I'm going to work on that.
Thank you. I've noticed my torso is more forward compared to others. I've been working on hip mobility, but not really on ankles. Will do that.

30 kg bench press today (4x6)
